stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $(A, \text{d})$ and $(B, \text{d})$
be differential graded algebras over $R$. Let $N$ be a
differential graded $(A, B)$-bimodule. The dg Hom construction $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_B(N,M)$ with its induced dg $A$-action
defines a functor
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, -) :
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}
\longrightarrow
\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}
$$
of differential graded categories. This functor induces functors
$$
\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})} \to \text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}
\quad\text{and}\quad
K(\text{Mod}_{(B, \text{d})}) \to K(\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})})
$$ by passing to closed degree-zero maps and homotopy classes.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring; A and B are dg R-algebras; N is a dg (A,B)-bimodule.
conclusions: The internal Hom functor Hom_B(N,-) defines a dg functor from dg right B-modules to dg right A-modules, and induces functors on ordinary dg-module and homotopy categories.

reason: For homogeneous f, composition with f defines an A-linear map between internal Hom complexes. Because dg-category composition is a chain map, the differential identity d(c_f)=c_(df) follows from the Leibniz rule, proving the internal Hom assignment is a dg functor.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $A$ and $B$ be $R$-algebras.
Let $M$ be a right $A$-module, $N$ an $(A, B)$-bimodule, and
$N'$ a right $B$-module. Then we have a canonical isomorphism
$$
\Hom_B(M \otimes_A N, N') = \Hom_A(M, \Hom_B(N, N'))
$$
of $R$-modules.
If $A$, $B$, $M$, $N$, $N'$ are compatibly graded, then we have a
canonical isomorphism
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_B^{gr}}(M \otimes_A N, N') =
\Hom_{\text{Mod}_A^{gr}}(M, \Hom_{\text{Mod}_B^{gr}}(N, N'))
$$
of graded $R$-modules
If $A$, $B$, $M$, $N$, $N'$ are compatibly differential graded, then
we have a canonical isomorphism
$$
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(M \otimes_A N, N') =
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(A, \text{d})}}(M,
\Hom_{\text{Mod}^{dg}_{(B, \text{d})}}(N, N'))
$$
of complexes of $R$-modules.
